content.text: {"label":"unknown_demand_surge","explanation":"General calls are running 34-51% above forecast since 10:15 (218 vs 153 in the last two intervals), and service level has fallen to 24.6%. AHT is close to forecast and attendance is normal: no general absences and only 1 payments sick call, below the usual level. So this is a demand problem, not a staffing problem. The rise is spread across most reasons: login_issue x1.76, balance_enquiry x1.4, other_general x1.3, loan x1.19. No customer-facing incident explains it; the only open incident is a P4 internal staff email delay. The 10:30 fraud-awareness social post also does not fit, because fraud_report calls are below normal. The cause is not established, so this is an unknown demand surge. Payments is also somewhat above forecast and its service level slipped to 60.9%.","plan_name":"General surge recovery: borrow break time, add overtime, deflect simple enquiries","rationale":"General needs roughly 12-15 extra agent-equivalents at the current excess. Payments is itself below 70% service level, so it cannot donate cross-skilled agents. The plan stacks levers in order of cost. First, delay breaks on both queues for the next two hours (free). Second, cancel non-mandatory general coaching for the midday period. Third, offer consecutive overtime blocks on general: about 6 accepted agents per block, roughly Rs 8,600 in total, within the Rs 15,000 budget. Fourth, deflect 20% of balance_enquiry and new_offer_enquiry calls to chat at Rs 12 per chat. Finally, turn on IVR callback on general to cut abandonment and spread the peak.
